Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 5, Verse 27

“Shutting out external contacts, fixing the gaze between the brows, making even the inward and outward breaths that move through the nostrils...”

The chapter turns suddenly practical, giving posture and breath. Krishna has argued philosophically for twenty-six verses and now hands over something to actually do, as though the argument were only ever clearing ground for this.
